Solid Waste Disposal
Rehabilitation, demolition and clearance of deteriorated structures and neighborhood clean-up activities will generate a significant amount of solid waste and debris. The volume of this material could be extremely variable and is not possible to estimate accurately. Due to the limited capacity of existing disposal sites it is possible that these programs will have a minor adverse impact by accelerating the rates at which available disposal sites are filled. Salvaging and recycling of reusable material would also serve to mitigate adverse impacts resulting from the proposed rehabilitation and conservation projects.
Fire and Police Protection Services
In rehabilitating deteriorated structures, removing critically deficient units and cleaning up neighborhood debris the programs will reduce existing fire hazards. Inadequate and defective wiring, structural deficiencies and accumulated rubbish create conditions which are conducive to fire and contribute to the need and demand for fire protection service.
By providing street lighting and otherwise physically changing residential neighborhoods which contain extensive structural deterioration and physical blight, the rehabilitation projects are expected to improve the quality of the human environment in the respective target areas. It is probable that some decrease in the need and demand for police protection will occur. The rehabilitation programs will have a positive impact on both of these services both locally in the target areas and in the community in general.
Schools
The C.D.B.G. neighborhood revitalization programs will not increase residential densities in any area. Therefore no increase in student population can be anticipated. The upgrading and preservation of older residential areas will however encourage families with school-age children to remain in these residential areas rather than relocating to newer vicinities in the city. To this degree the C.D.B.G. programs will have a positive impact, keeping children in older established schools with stable or declining enrollments rather than those students moving into school districts experiencing overcrowded conditions.
Parks and Streets
Reconstruction, resurfacing, drainage, curbs, and sidewalks and other street improvements will enhance the level of service in the affected neighborhoods, especially improving services which depend heavily on the street system for their efficient discharge. This is not only true for fire, police and refuse collection, but also applies to utilities such as gas, electricity, water and city maintenance activities whose functions require mobility. The most noticeable impact will occur in Alviso where the street system is most deficient.
